About me

I develop mathematical and computational models of complex systems. My primary field is ecology and evolution; the same tools travel to sustainability and socioeconomic questions.

I am a PhD researcher at the University of Groningen, in the Theoretical Research in Evolutionary Life Sciences (TRÊS) cluster, working with Rampal Etienne (Theoretical and Evolutionary Community Ecology) and Sander van Doorn (Evolutionary Systems Biology). My doctoral project, The evolutionary consequences of isolation, asks how limited immigration reshapes the emergence, persistence and evolution of ecological communities. It is funded by an EVOLVE fellowship (EU MSCA COFUND).

Before Groningen I trained in marine science at the University of the Aegean and in applied ecological and evolutionary sciences at the University of Montpellier, with research at UMR MARBEC on regime shifts and functional diversity in Mediterranean fish communities. Earlier, I spent several years monitoring marine biodiversity and species invasions through citizen science with the environmental organisation iSea and in collaboration with international institutes such as the Marine & Environmental Research (MER) Lab and the Hellenic Centre for Marine Research (HCMR).

Alongside the PhD I coordinate the SDSN Youth Greece network and work with the Political Economy of Sustainable Development Lab at the University of Athens on climate-change reporting. That work applies systems thinking to organisations and institutions rather than to species.

I speak Greek, English and French. I am based in Groningen, Netherlands.
